title: DAR GLOBAL'S ICONIC PROJECTS TIERRA VIVA IN SPAIN, AIDA IN OMAN, AND LES VAGUES IN QATAR ENTER THE CONSTRUCTION PHASE ON THE BACK OF SURGING INVESTOR DEMAND
text:
DAR GLOBAL'S ICONIC PROJECTS TIERRA VIVA IN SPAIN, AIDA IN OMAN, AND LES VAGUES IN QATAR ENTER THE CONSTRUCTION PHASE ON THE BACK OF SURGING INVESTOR DEMAND
DUBAI, UAE, Dec. 15, 2023 /PRNewswire/ -- Dar Global, the luxury international real estate developer, has announced a significant milestone as it simultaneously begins construction on three of its much-anticipated projects in December 2023 - Tierra Viva in Spain, AIDA in Oman, and Les Vagues in Qatar.
The commencement of construction activity on the three standout developments reflects Dar Global's unwavering commitment to delivering high-caliber projects on time to maximise long-term value for investors. The landmark addresses redefine luxury living experiences and further solidifies the brand's regional and global presence following its successful listing on the London Stock Exchange earlier this year.
Having delivered a strong financial performance in H1 2023 and expanding its portfolio of assets with the announcement of three new luxury brand partnerships, Dar Global continues to set new benchmarks in the global real estate arena with its ambitious growth strategy.

title: DAR GLOBAL'S ICONIC PROJECTS TIERRA VIVA IN SPAIN, AIDA IN OMAN, AND LES VAGUES IN QATAR ENTER THE CONSTRUCTION PHASE ON THE BACK OF SURGING INVESTOR DEMAND
text:
Ziad El Chaar, CEO of Dar Global, said: "We are excited to announce the commencement of construction across three of our most distinctive luxury developments. Tierra Viva, AIDA, and Les Vagues witnessed an overwhelming response from customers and investors, and Dar Global will continue to set new benchmarks for quality and exclusivity as we deliver these top-tier properties in line with our scheduled project timelines. In H1 2023, we recorded strong demand for both newly launched and existing projects, and we are excited to close the year on a high note as we progress as scheduled on these prestigious projects amid surging interest from investors worldwide."
Located within the ultra-exclusive locality of Benahavis and with a GDV of c. €282 million, Tierra Viva marks Dar Global's and Automobili Lamborghini's first project in continental Europe and is inspired by the iconic design of the legendary Automobili Lamborghini.
Developed as a joint venture with Omran Group, the Sultanate of Oman's executive arm for tourism development, AIDA represents Oman's largest urban development. The commencement of the first phase of construction on its site marks a crucial step in transforming the landscape and bringing the vision of AIDA to life.
Les Vagues, the ﬁrst ever branded residential project in Qatar with interiors by ELIE SAAB, is valued at 1 billion Qatari Riyal. The start of the main construction activity marks a significant milestone for Les Vagues.

title: DAR GLOBAL AND THE TRUMP ORGANISATION EXPAND SAUDI PORTFOLIO WITH USD 1BN TRUMP PLAZA JEDDAH
text:
JEDDAH, Saudi Arabia, Jan. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Dar Global (LSE: DAR), the London-listed international luxury real estate developer, announced today the official launch of Trump Plaza Jeddah, marking its third prestigious collaboration with The Trump Organization in Saudi Arabia. Valued at over USD 1 billion, this landmark development, strategically located within the expansive Amaya development along King Abdulaziz Road, is poised to redefine luxury urban living in Jeddah's thriving real estate landscape, following the successful launch of Trump Tower Jeddah in December 2024.
Residential offerings include fully furnished 1, 2, and 3-bedroom Trump Executive Residences; premium 2, 3, and 4-bedroom Trump Park Residences; and exclusive 4-bedroom Trump Townhouses. Together with thoughtfully designed home offices, premium retail, and curated dining, the project redefines modern living by blending convenience and luxury into a single, connected destination. Optional rental management services further enhance the appeal for international owners seeking a turnkey ownership experience.

title: DAR GLOBAL AND THE TRUMP ORGANISATION EXPAND SAUDI PORTFOLIO WITH USD 1BN TRUMP PLAZA JEDDAH
text:
Eric Trump, Executive Vice President of The Trump Organization, commented: "Expanding our presence in Saudi Arabia with Trump Plaza Jeddah underscores our commitment to world-class quality and iconic design. This project reflects the strength of our relationship with Dar Global and our confidence in Jeddah as a dynamic, globally relevant city. Trump Plaza Jeddah will set a new benchmark for integrated urban destinations."
Ziad El Chaar, CEO of Dar Global, added: "The launch of Trump Plaza Jeddah represents a major milestone in our Saudi portfolio. This is not a single-use development, but a carefully curated urban ecosystem designed for global residents who want to live, work, and connect within the best address in Jeddah. Anchored by a private park and supported by world-class amenities, Trump Plaza Jeddah introduces a new model for modern city living in the Kingdom."
Central to the lifestyle offering is the exclusive 4,000-square-metre Vitality Club, with golf simulators, a spa, sports medicine and recovery facilities, swimming pools, dining, and high-performance wellness spaces. Destination retail and dining, including Trump Grill, Trump Daily, an artisan bakery, and a fitness pro shop, reinforce its positioning as a district day and night.

title: Dar Global launches $267m project in Jeddah amid Saudi expansion push | The National
text:
London-listed real estate developer Dar Global is launching a new mixed-use development in Jeddah, with an estimated value of about 1 billion Saudi riyals ($267 million) as part of its expansion plans in the kingdom.
The project will be developed on a plot of land acquired for $56 million and forms part of Dar Global's programme to expand its Saudi Arabia portfolio by up to 4 billion riyals, the company said on Monday.
On completion of the programme, the company's worldwide development pipeline is expected to reach about $24 billion, it added.
A new international luxury brand will be introduced to Jeddah as part of the development, as the company plans to announce more land acquisitions in the kingdom.
Dar Global has partnerships with more than 10 brands, including the Trump Organisation, Aston Martin, Automobili Lamborghini, Missoni, Pagani Automobili and W Hotels, among others at its developments.
“With buyers from 61 nationalities already investing in our Saudi portfolio, we are witnessing accelerating international confidence in the country's real estate sector,” said Ziad El Chaar, chief executive of Dar Global. “This new development marks another significant milestone in our global expansion strategy.”
The Arab world’s largest economy is looking to boost home ownership for Saudi citizens as part of its Vision 2030 programme. It has also opened up the property sector to foreign ownership, a move expected to attract increased demand.

title: Dar Global launches $267m project in Jeddah amid Saudi expansion push | The National
text:
However, buyers remained “selective” in the kingdom during the third quarter amid regional uncertainty triggered by Iran war, a recent report by JLL said.
In the July to September period, sale transaction volumes in Riyadh fell by about 30 per cent year-on-year to 9,100, while values decreased 51.8 per cent to 8.5 billion riyals.
Residential transaction volumes in Jeddah fell by 25.8 per cent on an annual basis to 3,100. Transaction values fell by 5.8 per cent to 3.9 billion riyals, JLL said.
With a presence in 14 international cities across nine countries, Dar Global’s portfolio of 4,200 units completed or under construction, spans the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Oman, Qatar, the UK, Spain and Greece.
It is building three residential projects in Saudi Arabia in partnership with the Trump Organisation, including a $1 billion Trump Tower in Jeddah and a Trump-branded luxury project in Wadi Safar in the capital.
Dar Global and the US President are also in partnership for the development of a $1 billion Trump Tower on Dubai's Sheikh Zayed Road.
Other international developers, including UAE-based Arada, are also expanding to Saudi Arabia.
Last month, Arada unveiled a Dh14 billion ($3.8 billion) residential project in Riyadh, with plans to build 100,000 homes in Saudi Arabia over the next three to five years.
Up to 3,500 villas and townhouses will be built in Al Rimal district in Riyadh's north-eastern growth corridor on a 2.5 million-square-metre plot.

title: Seven projects, four countries: Mapping Trump’s Gulf property empire | The National
text:
From an 80-storey tower on Dubai’s Sheikh Zayed Road to golf resorts in Saudi Arabia, Qatar and Oman, the Trump name is appearing on a growing number of high-profile developments in the Gulf.
The Trump Organisation now has six projects worth billions of dollars under development across four Gulf countries, as the US President’s brand expands its presence in one of the world’s most lucrative property markets.
The group, which completed its first Gulf project – Trump International Golf Club in Dubai – with UAE developer Damac in 2017, has developments under way in Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Qatar and Oman. These include golf courses, hotels and luxury residences in Dubai, Riyadh, Jeddah, Doha and Muscat.
The six projects are being developed with Dar Global, the international property arm of Saudi Arabia-listed Dar Al Arkan.
In an interview with The National in 2024, Trump Organisation executive vice president Eric Trump said “the region loves our family, and the region loves our projects”.
“We were one of the first western brands to go into Dubai when no one else really believed, and everybody was a little sceptical, and everybody was a little cynical,” he said.
“We planted the Trump flag right there in the middle of the city. We did one of the greatest golf courses that's become, by far, the most successful golf venture anywhere in the Middle East … we’ve had such a great relationship with this region for so long, and I think we're going to keep on expanding.”
Jeddah-Riyadh

title: Seven projects, four countries: Mapping Trump’s Gulf property empire | The National
text:
Saudi Arabia is at the centre of the expansion. Three projects are being built in the kingdom: two in Jeddah and another at Wadi Safar in the capital, Riyadh, in partnership with Diriyah Company.
Together, the developments will feature Trump-branded golf courses, international hotels and premium residences, including apartments and town houses. The projects are scheduled for completion between 2029 and 2030.
This is as demand for homes in Saudi Arabia is projected to rise as it prepares to host the Fifa World Cup in 2034 and the World Expo in 2030.
The Arab world’s largest economy is looking to boost home ownership for Saudi nationals as part of its Vision 2030 initiative. It has also opened the property sector to foreign ownership, which is expected to further increase demand.
The Trump Organisation also launched a project in Qatar last year. The development in Doha covers about 790,000 square metres within the eight million-square metre Simaisma development, with an 18-hole Trump International Golf Course, a Trump Golf Clubhouse, and branded villas.
Dubai
Dubai is home to one of the biggest projects in the group’s Gulf portfolio.
In the UAE, the Trump Organisation and Dar Global are developing the $1 billion Trump Tower on Dubai's Sheikh Zayed Road. As well as 500 homes, the 80-storey development will have a Trump-branded hotel and an exclusive private members' club. The project is 80 per cent sold to a combination of regional and global investors.

title: Seven projects, four countries: Mapping Trump’s Gulf property empire | The National
text:
The tower is rising against the backdrop of a UAE property market where prices are still climbing, although growth has started to cool.
Dubai residential prices, grew by about 1.9 per cent annually in the second quarter of this year, with apartment prices increasing by 1.3 per cent and villas by 5.7 per cent, consultancy CBRE said.
Interest in taking the Trump brand into new markets also extends beyond the Middle East.
Dubai-based family business Abdulla Ali bin Haidar Group is negotiating with the Trump Organisation to build a luxury tourism complex in Santa Maria Island, east of Cuba's capital Havana.
The private conglomerate signed a letter of intent with the Cuban government for the Trump Island project but the Trump Organisation is yet to approve it.
Muscat
Oman completes the Trump Organisation’s current four-country Gulf footprint. The Trump Organisation and Dar Global are expanding with the development of a resort in the capital, Muscat, that will consist of villas, a hotel and a golf course.
The new Arabian Gulf developments are helping to boost Trump Organisation revenue, official data shows.
In a mandatory filing to the US Office of Government Ethics this year, President Donald Trump and the Trump Organisation reported that developers paid them $38 million in licensing fees for projects in Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the UAE.
Millions in licensing revenue

title: Seven projects, four countries: Mapping Trump’s Gulf property empire | The National
text:
The Trump brand is selling in the region, with President Trump reporting about $21.9 million in revenue from Dar Al Arkan last year, about the same as he reported in his 2024 financial disclosure.
Included in the most recent filing is $5.25 million that he received as a licence fee from the upcoming golf club and resort project in Doha.
The financial disclosure also showed that the US President reported millions of dollars in income from Damac.
Dar Global, listed on the London Stock Exchange, had a portfolio of $19 billion by the end of last year.
Overall the global expansion is driving strong financial returns. Dar Global's net profit for 2025 surged more than sixfold to $100.8 million and revenue more than doubled to $538.6 million, its financial statement shows.
Beyond the Middle East, The Trump Organisation is also active in the US, India, Indonesia, the Philippines, South Korea, Turkey and Uruguay.
Last year, it was reported that Syria had offered Donald Trump the opportunity to build a 45-storey luxury tower in Damascus in partnership with a UAE-based developer. However, the Trump Organisation did not confirm the reports.
The prospect comes as Syria seeks foreign investment to rebuild its economy following the US decision to remove the country from its list of state sponsors of terrorism.
For now, the Gulf remains at the heart of the Trump Organisation’s international expansion, and with six projects already under way, its footprint in the region is still growing.

title: Dar Global brings Trump Tower to Jeddah
text:
Trump development aims to cater to the luxury Saudi market and international investors
Dubai: Dar Global, the Dubai-based property developer listed on the london stock exchange (LSE), partners with The Trump Organisation to bring the Trump Tower to the Jeddah.
This venture marks their second collaboration following the recent announcement of the Trump International Oman project, part of the AIDA development—a $500 million (Dh1.8 billion) mixed-use real estate initiative.
The Jeddah project signifies Dar Global's debut in the city, expanding beyond its role as the global arm of Saudi Arabia’s largest developer, Dar Al Arkan. According to Dar Global, the Trump development aims to cater to the luxury Saudi market and appeal to international investors.
Since its listing on the LSE in February last year, Dar Global has amassed a portfolio pipeline valued at $5.9 billion (Dh21.6 billion), with nearly half of that designated for projects in the GCC, as stated by CEO Ziad El Chaar.

title: Meed
text:
Dar Global to develop $4.2bn Oman mixed-use project
10 December 2025
Register for MEED’s 14-day trial access
Saudi Arabia-headquartered real estate developer Dar Global has announced that it will develop a mixed-use project in Muscat at an estimated investment of RO1.6bn ($4.2bn).
Dar Global will co-develop the Muscat Marine, Art & Digital District project with Oman's Art District Real Estate Development Company.
The project will cover an area of over 1.5 million square metres (sq m) and will be developed in several phases over 12 years.
The development will comprise a mix of residential communities, cultural venues, marinas, retail spaces, finance and business parks and hotels.
Dar Global, a subsidiary of Dar Al-Arkan, was one of the first Saudi brands to list on the London Stock Exchange.
Dar Al-Arkan established Dar Global in 2017 to focus on developing projects in the Middle East and Europe, including in Dubai, Qatar, Oman, London and the Costa del Sol in southern Spain.
Dar Global has $12bn-worth of projects under development in six countries: the UAE, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, the UK and Spain.
It completed three developments – the Urban Oasis and Da Vinci towers in Dubai and the Sidra gated community in Bosnia – in 2023.
The company collaborates with global brands including Missoni, W Hotels, Versace, Elie Saab, Automobili Pagani and Automobili Lamborghini.

title: Meed
text:
In Oman, Dar Global is also developing the Aida project. In May, it awarded a contract to develop the villas and apartments as part of the project.
According to an official statement, the construction works are expected to start immediately and the project is slated for completion in 2026.
The main contract was awarded to local firm Al-Adrak Trading & Contracting.
The latest announcement follows the awarding of contracts in June last year for the development of the first phase of the Aida project.
The Aida project is being developed as a joint venture with Omran Group and the first phase is expected to be completed in 2027.
UK analytics firm GlobalData forecasts that the Omani construction industry will expand at an annual average growth rate of 4.2% in 2025-28. Growth in the country will be supported by rising government investments in renewable energy, the transport infrastructure and the housing sector, all as part of Oman's Vision 2040 strategy.
Growth during the forecast period will also be supported by increasing hospitality sector investments, with the government planning to invest RO11.9bn ($31bn) in tourism development projects by 2040 and supporting the construction of several hospitality projects.

title: Meed
text: Hydrom targets hyperscalers in round four 19 November 2026 Oman’s green hydrogen company Hydrom is turning to domestic demand to support the sector as export markets slow, says managing director Abdulaziz Al-Shidhani. Speaking to MEED after Hydrom awarded two projects under its third auction round and launched a fourth round linked to data centres at UN climate change conference Cop31 in Antalya, Al-Shidhani says interest in the third round had been satisfactory but below earlier levels. “There was a good interest, satisfactory to the auction itself, but it was not as big as it was in round one specifically,” he says. “[That is] reflecting the overall market sentiment when it comes to green hydrogen.” Hydrom does not disclose the number of auction bids it receives. Domestic demand According to Al-Shidhani, regulatory slowdowns in Europe and slower progress in markets such as South Korea and Japan prompted Hydrom to look for buyers at home. “We decided last year to start exploring each and every avenue domestically to support decarbonising our industries and introducing green solutions for expanding the industrial base within Oman itself,” he says. Steel, methanol, mobility, hydrogen-to-power and data centres are among the applications that are under review. A natural gas supply agreement was recently signed for a green direct reduced iron (DRI) plant, which carries a mandate to replace natural gas with green hydrogen in the early 2030s. Hydrom is helping first-round developers in Duqm reach a commercial agreement with the DRI investor. Data centres The fourth round, the Green-Powered Data Centre Hydrogen Auction, will be held in Dhofar Governorate. The city of Salalah was chosen for its connectivity, cooler climate and seawater cooling. Al-Shidhani says the national grid is not yet in a position to supply hyperscalers requiring 100MW or more. The Energy & Minerals Ministry and the Transport, Communications & Information Technology Ministry mandated Hydrom to design a captive power solution. “Our work yielded that the best techno-commercial proposition is a blend of renewable electrons supported by batteries and supported by up to 20% firming power through hydrogen gensets,” he says. The auction is designed for integrated consortiums covering power, hydrogen and data centre hubs. Hydrom will also offer matchmaking for investors that want a partner to supply the energy. Registration for expressions of interest is open until February 2027. Al-Shidhani says a market sounding exercise had given “a very positive signal”. Hydrom plans to issue the request for qualification by the end of the first quarter of 2027, with requests for proposals expected around mid-year. Round three The awards went to a consortium of Petrogas E&P and Italy’s Bio3Energy, which plans to produce about 625,000 tonnes a year (t/y) of green ammonium nitrate, and a consortium of PLN Indonesia Power Renewables, Alawi Enterprises and HBA Offshore International, which plans to produce about 400,000 t/y of green ammonia. Combined green hydrogen output is expected to reach about 121,000 t/y by 2032. The block offered covers 300 square kilometres and could accommodate up to three projects. One winner has an option on a further 100 square kilometres, which would use the full block. Al-Shidhani says the land usufruct agreements will be registered with Oman’s Housing Ministry within two to three weeks. Developers then have three and a half years for development work, with a final investment decision expected by the end of year three and financial close six months later. Construction is allotted three and a half years, followed by 40 years of operations. He says the 2032 production date does not represent a delay to Oman’s 2030 target. “It is a rolling process,” he says. “The 2030 [projects] were signed in 2023 and 2024. It is a moving target.” One of the new projects has opted for solar power only at the outset. Hydrom does not specify generation or electrolyser technology. Project finance remains the most common funding route, although Al-Shidhani says export credit agencies could also play a role. This is a demonstration that Oman is able to produce [some of] the lowest-cost hydrogen First production The first phase of India-based Acme Group’s project in Duqm, which will produce 100,000 t/y of green ammonia, is expected to start production in Q2 2027. Al-Shidhani, who visited the site in October, says major components were almost complete. “This is a demonstration that Oman is able to produce [some of] the lowest-cost hydrogen and deliver it competitively to markets, and we are not talking about small quantities,” he says. He expects the first export cargo to convince sceptical investors that Oman can produce hydrogen for less than $3 a kilogram. Other first- and second-round developers are still negotiating offtake before moving to front-end engineering and design. Further rounds Al-Shidhani says the awarded projects use approximately 4% of the land available to Hydrom, and that further auctions are certain. Oman’s strategy targets 8.5 million t/y of green hydrogen by 2050. Hydrom paused for almost a year after the second auction round, and the timing of future rounds will depend on the market. “It is all about selecting the right time to go to the market,” he says. “In terms of whether there would be round five or round six, the answer is definitely there would be.” https://image.digitalinsightresearch.in/uploads/NewsArticle/21573009/main.gif

                            Contractors submit best offers for Oxagon Highway 55 19 November 2026 Contractors have submitted their best and final offers for a design-and-build contract to upgrade Highway 55 in Saudi Arabia’s Oxagon region. The first phase of the project includes the construction of 14 kilometres of road, with two lanes in each direction, as well as one bridge and three interchanges. The project is expected to take 22 months to complete. Contractors initially submitted bids on 28 September, as MEED exclusively reported. Highway 55 connects the Red Sea coast with the mainland in northwestern Saudi Arabia. It is currently the only road providing north-south connectivity between Duba and the Neom region. MEED reported exclusively in August last year that contractors had submitted responses to an expression of interest notice that Neom had issued earlier that month. The project is expected to support cargo movement from Duba Port to other parts of the kingdom and the wider region. Last year, Neom tested a pilot initiative by handling a shipment that travelled from Cairo via the Port of Safaga, across the Red Sea to the Port of Neom, and then inland to Erbil, Iraq. In a statement, Neom said: “The shipment travelled through an intermodal corridor spanning over 900 kilometres, marking a significant milestone in the kingdom’s transformation into a regional and global logistics hub.”

text: Construction starts on Damascus hotel and mall 19 November 2026 Construction has started on the Movenpick Hotel and Arab Mall development in the Kafr Sousa district of Damascus. Rotana Star Holding and Sankari Holding are backing the project, which Syria’s Ministry of Tourism is developing under its patronage. The project marks Accor’s entry into the Syrian market. The France-based hotel group signed an agreement earlier this year to manage the project’s Movenpick Hotel component. The integrated development will cover more than 90,000 square metres (sq m) and combine hotel, retail, entertainment and supporting facilities. The Movenpick Hotel will occupy more than 25,000 sq m and include 300 accommodation units. Facilities will include event and celebration halls, restaurants with panoramic views, and health and fitness amenities. Arab Mall will cover more than 65,000 sq m across seven levels. It will include retail units, entertainment facilities and service areas. The developers expect Arab Mall to open in the first quarter of 2028, followed by the hotel in the first quarter of 2029. Accor acquired the Swiss-founded Movenpick brand in 2018. Under the management agreement, Accor will operate the hotel and provide access to its global reservation, distribution and marketing platforms. The development is expected to create direct and indirect employment across construction, engineering, hospitality, retail and services. The project is being advanced as Syria seeks to expand its tourism and hospitality capacity. Syria’s Ministry of Tourism has reported that the country received 3.52 million visitors in the first half of 2026, 111% more than in the same period of 2025. The ministry said foreign tourist arrivals increased by 448%, while Arab visitor numbers rose by 107%.

                            Kuwait discusses retender of $7.7bn of oil projects 19 November 2026 State-owned upstream operator Kuwait Oil Company (KOC) is discussing the retendering of upstream projects worth an estimated $7.7bn, according to industry sources. The tender processes for all four contracts were cancelled earlier this year after the lowest bids exceeded the projects’ approved budgets. The projects are: 
  - Separation Gathering Centre 1 (SGC-I) and Water Injection Plant (WIP-1)
Previous low bidder: Tecnicas Reunidas (Spain) – $2.47bn
  - Separation Gathering Centre 3 (SGC-3) and Water Injection Plant (WIP-3)

title: Meed
text:
Previous low bidder: Larsen & Toubro (India) – $2.48bn
  - Installation of Water Injection Plant (WIP-4)
Previous low bidder: Petrofac (UK) – $1.48bn
  - Effluent Water Disposal Plants 1 & 2 expansion project (EWDP 1&2)
Previous low bidder: Larsen & Toubro (India) – $1.30bn
KOC is considering a strategy under which pipeline and network installation work would be removed from the main contract scopes and tendered separately, the sources said. The company is also planning to relaunch the four main packages under a build-own-operate model rather than the engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) model used previously. KOC is expected to tender the pipeline and network packages on an EPC basis, or under a similar delivery model. In addition, KOC is discussing increases to the projects’ approved budgets to enable contractors to submit compliant bids, the sources said. Since KOC cancelled the four tenders in January, Kuwait’s oil and gas sector and the wider economy have faced disruption linked to the regional conflict that began after the US and Israel attacked Iran on 28 February. The conflict has reduced shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, limiting Kuwait’s ability to export crude oil.

text: Saudi Arabia cancels more water tenders 19 November 2026 Two tenders for a major water pipeline project in Saudi Arabia have been cancelled, marking the second major water infrastructure project in the kingdom to have its tender process called off this month. The tenders cover Package B and the combined Packages C1 and C3 of the New Water Pipeline to Feed Riyadh City 2 project, being developed by Water Transmission Company (WTCO). A source close to the project told MEED that bidders were notified of the decision earlier in November. The three packages have a combined value of about $556m and involve the construction of a long-distance potable-water transmission system to strengthen supplies to Riyadh. The wider masterplan includes approximately 136 kilometres of pipeline, with diameters ranging from 64 inches to 100 inches. The scope also includes 10 steel storage tanks with capacities ranging from 100,000 cubic metres to 170,000 cubic metres. According to regional tracker MEED Projects, Saudi Services for Electro-Mechanic Works was appointed as the main contractor for Package B in 2025, with a reported contract value of $279.6m. Another local firm, Al-Rawaf Trading & Contracting, was appointed for Packages C1 and C3, with a combined contract value of $276m. Multiple other contractors submitted bids for the three packages. As MEED understands, construction was expected to start earlier this year. The cancellations follow the withdrawal of a tender for a 300-million-litres-a-day seawater reverse osmosis desalination plant at Yanbu, valued at $272m. As reported by MEED on 16 November, Saudi Water Authority cancelled the Yanbu tender despite India’s VA Tech Wabag receiving the contract award in July 2025. The contractor disclosed the decision in a filing to Indian stock exchanges, saying the tender was cancelled due to “internal reasons” on the authority’s side. It is the second time a tender has been cancelled for the project at the final award stage. It is unclear whether the desalination or transmission-pipeline projects will be retendered and, if so, whether their scopes will remain unchanged. MEED has contacted WTCO for comment.

title: Dar Global posts solid H1 results; revenue up 66pc
text:
Dar Global, the London-listed luxury international real estate developer, recently announced its unaudited interim results for the six months ended June 30, 2026 reporting a 66% jump in its revenue hitting $258 million over last year's figure of $155.4 million.
The performance was driven by the Group’s projects and sustained demand across its diversified portfolio in the GCC, Europe, and UK.
Gross profit for the period rose 85% to $87.7 million, expanding margins to 34% (from 31%). Ebitda increased 73% to $46.3 million, while net profit surged 149% to $30.4 million over $12.2 million. Growth was primarily anchored by revenue recognition from landmark projects, including The Astera, Interiors by Aston Martin and Neptune, Interiors by Mouawad.
The Group’s Gross Development Value (GDV) nearly doubled year-on-year to reach $23 billion, reflecting rapid portfolio expansion. Cumulative contracted sales rose to $3.9 billion across 4,380 units.
Dar Global maintained a robust balance sheet with a Net Asset Value of $613.3 million and total cash balances of $847.9 million (comprising $231.6 million free cash and $616.3 million restricted escrow), supporting total available liquidity of $579.3 million.

title: Dar Global posts solid H1 results; revenue up 66pc
text:
Operational momentum accelerated in Saudi Arabia with major project launches. In January, the Group partnered with The Trump Organization to launch Rayana, a 2.6 million sq m gated community in Diriyah featuring luxury mansions and a championship golf course, followed by a SAR338 million ($90 million) infrastructure contract award to Compass and Bin Omairah Company.
Dar Global also unveiled Trump Plaza Jeddah (GDV $383.6 million) and the adjacent Padel Living Residences (GDV $142 million) within the Amaya masterplan.
Capital management and project execution remained key focus areas. In April, the Group strengthened its financial flexibility by closing a $250 million syndicated term loan facility.
Following the period in August, Dar Global appointed Gulf Asia Contracting to execute podium construction for the 80-storey, a 350-m Trump International Hotel & Tower on Dubai's Sheikh Zayed Road.
On the solid results, CEO Ziad El Chaar said: "We have delivered a resilient performance through uncertain times in the region, supported by the quality of our international portfolio. Buyer demand across our markets remained robust, with cumulative contracted sales at June 30, 2026 of $3.9 billion.
"During the period we closed our $250 million facility, further strengthening our balance sheet and liquidity," stated El Chaar.

title: Dar Global posts solid H1 results; revenue up 66pc
text: "Looking ahead, we remain focused on growing our Gross Development Value across both existing and new growth markets, while maintaining a disciplined focus on execution and delivery. With a strong balance sheet, disciplined capital management and a healthy project pipeline, Dar Global is well positioned to continue creating long-term value for its stakeholders," he added.

title: Dar Global announces record portfolio growth and landmark expansion
text:
Dar Global announces record portfolio growth and landmark expansion
Dar Global PLC reported record gross development value growth in 2025 on Wednesday, citing expansion into Saudi Arabian developments, stock exchange reclassification, and financial services ambitions.
Dar Global’s annual revenue more than doubled to $538.6 million from $240.3 million the previous year. Its pretax profit multiplied to $112.7 million, up from $14.0 million.
Its portfolio GDV more than doubled to $19 billion from $7.5 billion. It credits ‘landmark project launches’ and land acquisitions in the Saudi cities of Riyadh and Jeddah, as well as in Oman.
It has been awarded the main construction contracts for many developments across the region, including Trump Plaza, in collaboration with US President Donald Trump’s the Trump Organisation, and a prominent development project with an expected GDV of $1.95 billion.
Chief Executive Officer Ziad El Chaar said: ‘With strong sales momentum, accelerating project execution, and a strategic foothold in Saudi Arabia ahead of its landmark opening to foreign investors, we remain resilient.
‘Despite the prevailing global uncertainties, we enter 2026 with conviction in our strategy and full confidence in our ability to drive sustainable growth and long-term value creation for our stakeholders.’

title: Dar Global announces record portfolio growth and landmark expansion
text:
In September, the UK Financial Conduct Authority approved Dar Global to be listed under the Equity Shares (Commercial Companies) category, making it the first Gulf Cooperation Council-based company to do so.
As previously reported, the company says it will further endeavour to prioritise financial flexibility by entering asset management. It has proposed the proposed acquisition of a licensed platform based in the Dubai International Finance Centre, saying it will expand their access to global capital.
Shares in the Dubai, United Arab Emirates-based luxury real estate developer fell 3.0% to 6.55 cents per share in London on Wednesday afternoon. Shares have been up 25% overall in the last 12 months.

Ziad El Chaar, the Vice Chairman at Wasalt, stated: “Today, with this accreditation from infath, Wasalt has further reaffirmed its leadership position, in offering seamless and specialized services, which ultimately results in a dynamic and distinctive auction experience.”
Wasalt offers a variety of online services for buying, selling, and renting properties across the Kingdom. It aims to provide users with a convenient and unique action experience.
Infath is a governmental center that seeks to establish cooperation between the judicial and governmental entities in areas of liquidations, sales and other assets that are not subjected to a current legal dispute.

title: Kite vs Wasalt
text:
Kite vs Wasalt
En bref
Wasalt est une plateforme immobilière axée sur l’Arabie saoudite, avec des profils d’agents et des annonces vérifiées. Kite regroupe les annonces de Wasalt avec celles de plus de 20 autres plateformes : vous voyez tout le marché, avec des analyses de prix pour savoir si l’offre est juste.
| Fonctionnalité | Kite | Wasalt | 
|---|---|---|
| Sources consultées | Plus de 20 plateformes | Ses propres annonces uniquement | 
| Détection des annonces multi-plateformes | Oui (badge « Aussi sur ») | Non | 
| Analyse des prix | Centiles, historique, comparables | Non | 
| Comparaison des quartiers | Données côte à côte | Non | 
| Profils d’agents | Non (liens vers la source d’origine) | Oui (agents vérifiés) | 
| Intégration IA (MCP) | Oui (serveur MCP) | Non | 
| Langues | 20 | 2 (arabe, anglais) | 
| Gratuit | Consultation gratuite ; connectez-vous pour voir les coordonnées | Consultation gratuite, compte requis pour publier | 
| Publication d’annonces | Non | Oui | 
| Application mobile | Web uniquement | Web + adapté au mobile | 
À qui s’adresse Kite
- Les locataires qui veulent voir TOUTES les annonces disponibles sur toutes les plateformes
- Toute personne qui veut savoir si un prix est juste
- Les expatriés qui ont besoin d’une interface multilingue
À qui s’adresse Wasalt
- Les agents qui veulent publier des biens avec un profil professionnel
- Les utilisateurs qui préfèrent un contact direct avec des agents vérifiés
Questions fréquentes

title: Kite vs Wasalt
text:
- Kite inclut-il les annonces de Wasalt ?
- Oui, Kite regroupe les annonces de Wasalt ainsi que celles de plus de 20 autres plateformes saoudiennes.
- Kite est-il gratuit ?
- Oui. Rechercher et comparer les annonces est gratuit et ne demande aucun compte. La connexion, gratuite elle aussi, affiche les coordonnées des annonceurs.
- Puis-je publier une annonce sur Kite ?
- Non, Kite est un agrégateur de recherche. Pour publier des annonces, utilisez directement Wasalt ou d’autres plateformes.
